interface.title: DF-XRM visualization (DF-XRM_viz v2.1.x, Streamlit)
interface.field: Materials physics / synchrotron X-ray imaging (dark-field X-ray microscopy)
interface.stage_of_work: Mainly experiment planning before beamtime (checking that a sample is viable and working out the alignment geometry). The tool's paper also names communicating the 3D geometry to collaborators and beamline staff, and using it during the experiment and in data analysis. This run exercised only the planning use.
interface.what_it_is_for: Pick a crystal, an X-ray energy and a sample size; check how much beam gets through the sample; choose an (hkl) reflection; then see the 3D sample–beam–lens–goniometer geometry, read off the goniometer angles and lens-box position, and export them as a record to share with the beamline team and keep in the experiment logbook.

data.note: Built-in crystals from the 'Or select a crystal structure' dropdown (Diamond, Aluminium, BaTiO3, KNbO3, LiNbO3, W, Pb, ...). Diamond was used for most of the run and W to show a sample that fails. The uploaded test file NaCl_rocksalt.cif was also loaded; it only takes effect when the dropdown is set back to 'Upload'. The lens box used was the built-in 'sample (id06@ESRF)'.

tree.general: Plan a diffraction-imaging experiment on a crystal and record its geometry for the team: check the sample lets enough beam through, choose a reflection, work out the instrument settings, and export them for the beamline staff and the experiment logbook
tree.specific: Plan a DF-XRM measurement: check attenuation and transmission, choose an (hkl) from the reflection table, read φ/χ/ω and the lens-box mount point, and export a PDF, Blender scene, .lens file or PNG

features.name: Crystal-structure loader
features.general: Pick a material from a built-in structure library or upload your own structure file, and see a summary of its formula, density and lattice parameters that feeds every downstream calculation
features.specific: 'Or select a crystal structure' dropdown (Diamond, Aluminium, BaTiO3, KNbO3, LiNbO3, W, Pb, ...) plus 'Upload a .cif file'; the page shows formula, density and a/b/c (e.g. Diamond C8, 3.516 g/cm³, a=3.567 Å; NaCl a=5.640 Å, 2.164 g/cm³). An uploaded .cif is ignored until the dropdown is set to 'Upload'; the uploader shifting the page can make the next dropdown click land on the wrong entry
steps: choose a crystal from the dropdown
or upload a .cif file and set the dropdown to 'Upload'
read the formula, density and lattice parameters
the attenuation plots, reflection table and geometry recompute for the new crystal
serves_tasks: Choose the material to study from a built-in library
Load your own material structure file

features.name: Material attenuation and transmission check, with linked energy/wavelength inputs
features.general: Given a material, a probe energy (entered either as energy or as wavelength, the other updating to match) and a thickness, plot attenuation length against energy and transmission against thickness, with markers at the chosen values, to decide whether enough beam gets through
features.specific: Crystal plus Energy [keV] / Wavelength [Å] plus Sample thickness drive two log plots: attenuation length [µm] vs energy with an 'E = … keV' line, and 'Transmission @ … keV' vs thickness with a '% transmitted' label. Energy and wavelength are linked (30 keV → 0.4133 Å, 0.5 Å → 24.7968 keV), and the plots, 2θ and reflection table recompute. Replay caveats: editing the wavelength raises a yellow Session State warning ('The widget with key "energy_kev" was created with a default value but also had its value set via the Session State API'), and changing the energy also changes the Q vector on its own
steps: choose a crystal (built-in or uploaded .cif)
enter the energy, or the wavelength (the other one updates)
enter the sample thickness
read the attenuation length and % transmission at the markers
change the material or energy and compare
serves_tasks: Check how much of the beam gets through the sample at the chosen settings, and compare materials and settings
Set the probe energy, either as energy or as wavelength

features.name: Sortable allowed-reflection table feeding a target selector
features.general: List the candidate reflections with their properties, sort by any column, then enter the chosen one as the target that drives the geometry
features.specific: Table of allowed (h,k,l) with 2θ, Intensity [%] and d-spacing [Å]; sort by clicking a header, then type the (h,k,l) into 'Q vector (h, k, l)'; alignment angles and 3D scene update. Clicking a row does not set Q. After a crystal change Q resets to the first row in the table's own order (lowest 2θ), which for NaCl was (-1,-1,-1) at 4.5%, not the brightest. Replay caveats: the sort is lost on the next rerun, and changing the energy resets Q, so re-check Q after any energy edit
steps: read the reflection table for the current crystal and wavelength
click a column header to sort (e.g. Intensity descending)
type the chosen (h,k,l) into the Q vector field
read the updated 2θ and goniometer angles
serves_tasks: Browse and rank the candidate reflections by a property
Set the chosen reflection as the one to align on

features.name: Crystal-orientation-to-goniometer-angle solver
features.general: From a target reflection and constraints on how the sample is mounted and how the beam leaves it, compute the rotation-stage angles needed to reach the diffraction condition, with an optional manual override
features.specific: Q vector + Sample 'up' + Exit surface + 'Minimize distance beam travels through sample' (or a manual 'Beam exit direction'), giving 'Instrument alignment on (hkl)': 2θ, φ, χ, ω. Replay caveat: an Exit surface parallel to Q (e.g. (1,0,0) with Q=(2,0,0)) gives φ/χ/ω = nan with no warning
steps: set the Q vector
set Sample 'up' as (h,k,l) or [u,v,w]
set the Exit surface direction (not parallel to Q)
optionally untick 'Minimize distance…' and type a Beam exit direction
read φ, χ, ω
serves_tasks: Read the instrument angles needed to align on the chosen reflection
Describe how the sample is cut and mounted, and see the angles update
Choose the beam path through the sample instead of letting the tool minimise it

features.name: Interactive 3D experiment-geometry scene with drawing options
features.general: A rotatable, zoomable 3D model of the setup (specimen, its internal structure, beams, optics, motion stages, labelled angles) with toggles and scale controls, exportable as an image
features.specific: Plotly 3D scene with the sample box and its dimensions, unit cell with a/b/c axes, incident and diffracted beams, k0/Q/kh vectors, and goniometer arcs labelled φ/χ/ω. 'Show DFXRM lens' adds the lens; 'Visualization options' gives sample scale, beam width/thickness, crystal structure scale/position, bonds, show text and more. The modebar camera saves a PNG. The camera view resets on every rerun
steps: view the scene after choosing crystal and Q
tick Show DFXRM lens
open Visualization options and change crystal scale or beam width
drag to rotate and use the wheel to zoom
press the camera icon to save a PNG
serves_tasks: Inspect the 3D experimental layout from different viewpoints
Adjust how the layout is drawn for readability
Save the optics configuration and a picture of the layout

features.name: Optics (lens-box) layout calculator
features.general: Choose or upload an optics configuration, enter the total source-to-detector distance in one of two conventions, and get a dimensioned diagram with distances, magnification and mount coordinates, and download the configuration
features.specific: Lensbox dropdown ('sample (id06@ESRF)') or a .lens upload; type 'd_tot = …' or 'd_tot' = …' [mm]; the diagram shows d1, dL, d2, d_tot, the primed projections, 2θ, M and 'Lens mount point: x, y'; 'Download .lens file' saves the TOML
steps: choose a lens box (or upload a .lens file)
type d_tot or d_tot' and press Enter
read the lens mount point x/y and magnification
download the .lens file
serves_tasks: Choose a predefined optics configuration and see where to mount it
Change the detector distance and see the optics layout recompute
Save the optics configuration and a picture of the layout

features.name: Session export (PDF report and Blender scene)
features.general: Bundle the current settings and figures into a report on request, as a record for the experiment logbook and collaborators, and export the 3D scene with an import script for an external renderer
features.specific: Tick 'make pdf' to build DF-XRM_vis.pdf, then press 'Download pdf'; also 'Download pickled 3d structure for blender' and 'Download blender import script'
steps: tick make pdf
wait for the rerun
press Download pdf
download the pickled 3D structure and the Blender import script
serves_tasks: Export a report of the session
Export the 3D scene to an external 3D tool
